channel.title: Crypto Record
channel.description: Crypto Record reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto market.

item.title: Circle says USDC reinvestment leaves 7 cents per revenue dollar
item.description: Circle says it kept seven cents of each USDC revenue dollar in H1 2026, as Coinbase backs a rival model that sends reserve income to partners after a fee.

item.title: Ledger reviews wallet sales after $93 million crypto drain
item.description: Ledger is reviewing reseller sales and device tamper defenses after an implant-linked drain; analysts traced about $93 million, which Ledger has not confirmed.

item.title: Ledger reviews sales controls after wallet implant theft
item.description: Ledger is reviewing how its wallets reach buyers after an implant in reseller units captured recovery phrases and sent them over LTE to attackers.

item.title: Coinbase and Marqeta team up on stablecoin-backed cards
item.description: Coinbase will custody stablecoins and convert them to fiat for Marqeta card programs, with Base handling settlement and businesses able to fund programs 24/7.

item.title: Funding a Protocol on Another Chain Starts With the Asset
item.description: Funding a protocol on another chain means moving the right asset to its network, keeping gas for fees, then depositing through the protocol’s own contract.

item.title: Why volatile swaps can fill worse
item.description: A swap can fill below its quote when pool prices move before execution; MEV searchers can add pressure, while minimum-output limits cap what you accept.

item.title: Why Swap Fees Drift Between Quote and Execution
item.description: Swap fee drift is the gap between a swap’s estimated and final costs, caused by changing pool prices, route fees, network gas and execution conditions.

item.title: Why a Cross-Chain Swap Can Wait on Destination Gas
item.description: A cross-chain swap can stay pending after its input arrives because validators still need to observe, execute and fund the destination-chain payout from the quoted output.

item.title: Why a Calldata Change Can Break a Signed Swap
item.description: A swap signature covers specific transaction bytes or typed fields; changing calldata can break that authorization or change execution when the signed fields leave it open.

item.title: Same Ticker, Different Token: What a Bridge Actually Moves
item.description: A bridge can create or release a token with the same ticker as another asset; the chain, contract address and route determine what you actually hold.

item.title: How Bridged Dogecoin Becomes Smart-Chain Liquidity
item.description: Bridged DOGE can trade in smart-chain pools only after a bridge issues a compatible token; learn the route, pool steps, costs and risks before adding liquidity.

item.title: Three checks before bridging to a contract wallet
item.description: A bridge can deliver tokens to an address without making its wallet ready to use them. Check the route, destination wallet and control rules first.

item.title: When Is a Crypto Deposit Usable on an Exchange?
item.description: A transaction can appear on a blockchain before an exchange credits it; learn how confirmations, network choice and exchange checks determine when you can use funds.

item.title: Why a Crypto Swap Can Have Two Transaction Hashes
item.description: A transaction hash points to one signed on-chain action; two hashes usually mark separate approval and swap steps, letting you check each result on its own.

item.title: How Account Abstraction Changes Treasury Operations
item.description: Account abstraction lets treasury teams encode approvals, batch payments and manage gas in a smart account, while custody and bridge risks need separate controls.

item.title: Should You Swap Before or After a Crypto Bridge?
item.description: The right order depends on bridge support, liquidity and destination fees; compare the full cost of swapping on either chain before you send funds.

item.title: Repaying synthetic asset debt across a Mantle bridge
item.description: A bridge moves tokens between Ethereum and Mantle, while the protocol records and clears synthetic debt; repay only after matching its chain and accepted asset.

item.title: Four Costs to Check Before Moving BTC to ETH
item.description: A faster BTC-to-ETH route can cost more through network fees, exchange spread, bridge charges and destination gas; compare usable ETH, not arrival time alone.

item.title: Pay a Contractor on the Chain They Prefer
item.description: Pay a contractor on their preferred chain by confirming the asset, network, address and amount, then checking fees, settlement and records before sending.

item.title: What Changes When a Lending Market Accepts New Collateral
item.description: When a lending market accepts new collateral, its contract gains rules for valuing, borrowing against and liquidating the asset; users must check limits.
